attachment.content:
- agent-browser: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, including navigating pages, filling forms, clicking buttons, taking screenshots, extracting data, testing web apps, or automating any browser task. Triggers include requests to "open a website", "fill out a form", "click a button", "take a screenshot", "scrape data from a page", "test this web app", "login to a site", "automate browser actions", or any task requiring programmatic web interaction. Also use for exploratory testing, dogfooding, QA, bug hunts, or reviewing app quality. Also use for automating Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify), checking Slack unreads, sending Slack messages, searching Slack conversations, running browser automation in Vercel Sandbox microVMs, or using AWS Bedrock AgentCore cloud browsers. Prefer agent-browser over any built-in browser automation or web tools.
- portless: Set up and use portless for named local dev server URLs (e.g. https://myapp.localhost instead of http://localhost:3000). Use when integrating portless into a project, configuring dev server names, setting up the local proxy, working with .localhost domains, or troubleshooting port/proxy issues.
- codecast: Get codecast dashboard and share links for current session (user)
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# VoxFusion

A local-first, offline-capable voice transcription desktop app. All transcription happens on-device using a Whisper V3 Large Turbo model — no servers, no accounts, no internet required after first-time model download.

## Packages

| Package                    | Description              | Stack                                                           |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@voxfusion/app`           | Desktop application      | Tauri v2, SolidJS, Tailwind CSS, TypeScript, whisper-rs, SQLite |
| `@voxfusion/marketingsite` | Public marketing website | Astro, TypeScript, Wrangler                                     |

## Prerequisites

- [Bun](https://bun.sh/) (v1.0+)
- [Rust](https://rustup.rs/) (for Tauri development)
- [CMake](https://cmake.org/) (required to build whisper-rs; on macOS: `brew install cmake`)

## Getting Started

### Install dependencies

```bash
bun install
```

### Development

```bash
bun run dev
```

Or run the app directly:

```bash
bun run --filter @voxfusion/app dev
```

Or run the marketing site directly:

```bash
bun run --filter @voxfusion/marketingsite dev
```

### Tauri Desktop App

For full Tauri development with the native window:

```bash
cd packages/app
bun run tauri:dev
```

### Build

```bash
bun run build
```

## How it works

On first launch, the app walks the user through onboarding:

1. Microphone permission
2. Accessibility permission (for typing transcribed text into other apps)
3. Microphone device selection
4. Hotkey configuration
5. **Whisper model download** (~1.5 GB, one-time, requires internet)
6. Try-it-out / learning step
7. Completion

After onboarding, the app is fully offline. All transcriptions and dictionary words are stored locally in a SQLite database under the app's data directory.

## Linting & Formatting

This project uses [Biome](https://biomejs.dev/) for linting and formatting.

```bash
bun run check        # lint + format
bun run check:fix    # auto-fix
bun run format       # format only
bun run lint         # lint only
bun run typecheck    # TypeScript type checking
```

## Contributing

VoxFusion is released under the MIT license. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
for setup instructions, pull request guidelines, and privacy expectations for
contributions.

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

### Overview

VoxFusion is a Bun/Turborepo monorepo with two packages:

- `@voxfusion/marketingsite` — Astro static marketing website.

### Running services

| Service | Command | Port | Notes |
|---------|---------|------|-------|
| App frontend (Vite) | `cd packages/app && bunx vite --host 0.0.0.0` | 1420 | SolidJS UI only; Tauri IPC unavailable in standalone browser mode |
| Marketing site (Astro) | `cd packages/marketingsite && bun run dev -- --host 0.0.0.0` | 4321 | Fully functional on Linux |
| Full Tauri app | `cd packages/app && bun run tauri:dev` | — | Requires macOS (Metal, accessibility, tray) |

### Lint / typecheck / build

Standard commands documented in `README.md` scripts section. Key notes:

- `bun run check` — runs Biome across the whole repo. The marketing site has pre-existing lint warnings (unused imports).
- `bun run --filter @voxfusion/app typecheck` — passes clean.
- `bun run --filter @voxfusion/marketingsite typecheck` — runs `astro check` which currently reports ~1098 errors because it type-checks the app's SolidJS TSX files via workspace references. This is a pre-existing issue.
- `bunx vite build` (from `packages/app`) — builds the frontend successfully on Linux.
- `bun run build` (from `packages/marketingsite`) — builds all 6 static pages successfully.

### Rust / Tauri backend on Linux

`cargo check` in `packages/app/src-tauri` **will fail** on Linux because:

1. `whisper-rs` is compiled with `features = ["metal"]` which requires macOS Metal framework.
2. Several dependencies (`core-graphics`, `objc2`, `objc2-app-kit`) are macOS-only.

For frontend-only development on Linux, use the Vite dev server directly (`bunx vite`). The Rust backend requires macOS for compilation.

### System dependencies (Linux)

Required for `cargo check` to proceed as far as possible (before the macOS-specific failure):

```
libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libxdo-dev libssl-dev libasound2-dev
```

Also requires `libstdc++.so` symlink: `sudo ln -sf /usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/13/libstdc++.so /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libstdc++.so`

### System dependencies (macOS)

Required for `bun dev` / Tauri builds (whisper-rs-sys uses CMake to compile whisper.cpp):

```
brew install cmake
```

Without CMake, `bun dev` fails during `whisper-rs-sys` with `is cmake not installed?`.

### Gotchas

- Rust toolchain must be ≥1.85 (edition 2024 support). Run `rustup update stable && rustup default stable`.
- The app frontend at localhost:1420 shows a loading spinner and never progresses in a browser because it waits for the Tauri IPC bridge. This is expected; UI component development still works by navigating directly to routes.
- `turbo dev` runs both packages' dev scripts concurrently (uses TUI mode).

<result># VoxFusion Rust Backend Audit Findings

All paths relative to `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/` unless absolute. Line numbers verified against current code.

## HIGH

1. **`src-tauri/Cargo.toml:62` + `src-tauri/src/handlers/apps.rs:238,270,347` — `panic = "abort"` makes every `catch_unwind` useless; a panic in plist/icns parsing or the objc2 frontmost-app path aborts the whole app in release builds.**
   `panic = "abort"` (Cargo.toml) vs `let result = panic::catch_unwind(|| plist::Value::from_file(&plist_path).ok()).ok()??;` (apps.rs:238). In release, any malformed `Info.plist`/`.icns` in `/Applications`, or an ObjC exception in `get_frontmost_app` (apps.rs:347) — which runs at the start of *every* dictation — kills the process instead of being contained.
   Fix: drop `panic = "abort"` from the release profile (or replace the `catch_unwind` guards with genuinely non-panicking parsing and objc2 exception handling via `objc2::exception::catch`). Severity: **high**.

2. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:87` — every error return after `state.is_recording.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst)` leaves the recorder latched "recording" forever.**
   Failures at lines 97/102/106 (`.ok_or("No default input device available")?`), 110 (`default_input_config()`), 115 (`WavWriter::create`), 187 (`Unsupported sample format`), and 190 (`stream.play()`) all `?`-return without resetting the flag, so every subsequent `start_recording_with_device` fails with "Recording is already in progress." until the frontend happens to call `stop` (which errors too, but resets the flag as a side effect at line 207).
   Fix: use a guard/`defer` that resets `is_recording` (and `app_handle`) on any error path, or only set the flag after the stream is successfully playing. Severity: **high**.

3. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:176` — the ~1.5 GB Whisper model is loaded from disk on every single transcription.**
   `let ctx = WhisperContext::new_with_params(&model_path, ctx_params)` runs inside `transcribe_audio`, adding multi-second model load + Metal init to every dictation, then throws the context away.
   Fix: cache the `WhisperContext` in Tauri managed state keyed by model id (it's `Send + Sync`; create a fresh `WhisperState` per call), invalidating on `set_active_model`. Severity: **high**.

4. **`src-tauri/src/listeners/system_key_watcher.rs:133–146` — every system-wide keydown's keycode is broadcast into the webview, a keylogger stream with no CSP protecting it.**
   `emit_keyboard_key_pressed` emits `keyboard-key-pressed { key_code }` for *all* global `KeyDown` events (only `isARepeat()` is filtered, line 138); keycodes map directly to characters. Combined with `"csp": null` (finding 5), any webview compromise can log everything the user types system-wide.
   Fix: match hotkey chords in Rust (or at minimum only emit while the settings "record hotkey" UI is active / only emit an allowlisted set of keycodes). Severity: **high**.

5. **`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:44` — `"csp": null` disables Content-Security-Policy entirely.**
   Any injected script in the webview can call every allowed IPC command (`read_audio_file`, `list_transcriptions`, keylog events) and exfiltrate to any origin.
   Fix: set a CSP restricted to `'self'` plus `https://eu.i.posthog.com` (and the Tauri IPC scheme). Severity: **high**.

6. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:121–124` — microphone disconnect / stream error mid-recording is swallowed by `eprintln!` and never surfaced; recording silently stalls while UI still shows "recording".**

23. **Analytics with no opt-out in a "local-first, privacy-focused" app: `src/lib/posthog.ts:25–39` initializes PostHog unconditionally (`initPostHog()` at `src/index.tsx:19`) and events fire on every app open, transcription, and settings change; payloads are metadata-only (verified — e.g. `TranscriptionCard.tsx:26` sends only `transcription_id`/`text_length`), but there is no settings toggle or consent.** Fix: add an analytics opt-out setting checked in `capture()`, and disclose in onboarding. Severity: medium.

24. **`src-tauri/src/lib.rs:143–148` — single-instance plugin registered inside `.setup()` with `let _ =` swallowing its error; Tauri docs require it to be the *first* plugin registered so a second instance exits before doing work, and a registration failure here is silently ignored.** Fix: move `tauri_plugin_single_instance::init` to the first `.plugin()` call on the builder and propagate the error. Severity: medium.

25. **`src-tauri/src/tray.rs:80,107` — `handlers::audio::list_audio_devices().unwrap_or_default()` runs CoreAudio device enumeration synchronously on the main thread inside the menu-event handler and the `settings-changed` listener (can block 100+ ms per invocation), and errors are silently discarded.** Fix: enumerate on a background thread and update menu items via the handle. Severity: medium.

26. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/apps.rs:560+ (`list_installed_apps`) — every call re-scans three directories and re-decodes every app's `.icns` → PNG → base64 data-URL (hundreds of apps, tens of MB of IPC JSON) with no cache.** Fix: cache results keyed by app path + mtime in managed state or on disk. Severity: medium.

27. **`src-tauri/capabilities/desktop.json:14` — `core:webview:allow-internal-toggle-devtools` is granted in the production capability for both windows.** Fix: move it to a dev-only capability (or rely on the `devtools` cargo feature gating alone and remove the permission). Severity: medium.

28. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/media.rs` — if the app crashes or quits between `mute_media_for_recording` and `restore_media_after_recording`, the user's system output stays muted; also if the default output device changes mid-recording, `set_output_muted(false)` (line 197 region) unmutes the *new* device, leaving the original muted.** Fix: restore mute state in `RunEvent::ExitRequested`/`Exit` (lib.rs:186–194), and remember the muted device id rather than re-resolving the default. Severity: medium.

29. **`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:50–53` — updater tries `https://github.com/voxfusion/voxfusion/...` first, a GitHub org that doesn't match the actual repo owner (`gregor-tokarev`); minisign pubkey pinning (line 55) prevents malicious updates, but a squatter can serve garbage `latest.json` and break/deny updates for all users.** Fix: remove endpoints for repos you don't control. Severity: medium.

## LOW

30. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:255` — `Local::now().format("%Y%m%d%H%M%S")` gives second-resolution filenames; two recordings within one second silently overwrite (`WavWriter::create` truncates).** Fix: add milliseconds or a UUID suffix. Severity: low.

31. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/db.rs:261`, `apps.rs:598`, `sites.rs:184` — update commands return `created_at: String::new()`, handing the frontend an empty timestamp.** Fix: `SELECT created_at` (or use `UPDATE ... RETURNING`). Severity: low.

32. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/db.rs:118+` — cursor pagination on `created_at < ?1` skips rows that share an identical RFC3339 timestamp with the cursor.** Fix: use `(created_at, id)` composite cursor. Severity: low.

33. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/db.rs:73` — `dictionary_words` is always read `ORDER BY created_at DESC` (db.rs:187, 291; whisper.rs:120) but the only index is on `word` (`idx_dictionary_words_word`), which no query uses.** Fix: index `created_at` instead (impact minimal at this table size). Severity: low.

34. **Logging strategy split: `tauri-plugin-log` is configured (lib.rs:112–123) but the transcription hot path logs via `eprintln!` (`whisper.rs:196,226,270,278`, `audio.rs:123`, `browser.rs:120,131,141`), so these lines never reach the log file in a bundled app — and `whisper.rs:270` prints the user's dictionary/prompt contents to stderr.** Fix: replace `eprintln!` with `log::debug!/warn!` and drop user-content from log lines. Severity: low.

35. **Duplicated logic: the decode→mono→linear-resample pipeline exists twice (`audio_processing.rs:12–63` vs `whisper.rs:31–70`), and `whisper.rs:118–133 fetch_dictionary_words` duplicates `db.rs:275–292 get_dictionary_prompt`.** Fix: extract a shared `audio_util` module and reuse the db helper. Severity: low.

36. **`audio_processing.rs:40–60` / `whisper.rs:52–66` — linear-interpolation downsampling from 44.1/48 kHz to 16 kHz with no anti-aliasing low-pass folds high frequencies into the speech band, degrading transcription accuracy.** Fix: use `rubato` (or request a 16 kHz input config from cpal when supported). Severity: low.

37. **Dependency hygiene: `Cargo.lock` carries duplicate major trees — `objc2` 0.5.2 + 0.6.3 and `core-foundation` 0.9.4 + 0.10.1 (older ones via cpal/enigo) — and `Cargo.toml:36` uses `tokio = { features = ["full"] }` when only rt, fs, process, time, macros are needed.** Fix: trim tokio features; accept or upstream-bump the transitive dupes. Severity: low.

38. **`src-tauri/src/tray.rs:100–137` — the `settings-changed` listener appends new microphone menu items but never removes entries for disconnected devices, and menu IDs are `format!("mic_{}", device.name)` so identically-named devices collide.** Fix: rebuild the submenu from the current device list each time. Severity: low.

39. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:22–45` — `RecordingState` is a global `Mutex<RecordingState>` whose every field is *also* an `Arc<Mutex<Option<...>>>`; double-layered locking obscures the state machine that caused finding 2.** Fix: flatten to one `Mutex<Option<ActiveRecording>>` holding writer/stream/path together. Severity: low.

40. **`src-tauri/src/listeners/system_key_watcher.rs:102` — `.expect("system key pressed state mutex poisoned")` inside the main-thread event monitor would abort the app (panic=abort); unreachable in practice but pointless risk.** Fix: `let Ok(mut pressed) = ... else { return; }`. Severity: low.

41. **`src-tauri/src/window.rs:29–53` — `show_or_create_main_window` swallows all errors (`if let Ok(window)`, `let _ = window.show()`); a failed window creation from tray/reopen produces no feedback or log.** Fix: log the error branch. Severity: low.

42. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/browser.rs:57–86` — `normalize_domain` hand-parses URLs and mangles IPv6 hosts (`[::1]:8080` → `[`); the `url` crate is effectively free here.** Fix: parse with `url::Url` and fall back to the manual path. Severity: low.

43. **`src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs` (~line 310) and parakeet path — `text.split_whitespace().count()` reports word_count = 1 for CJK transcriptions, skewing stored stats for the `zh` style the app explicitly supports.** Fix: count Unicode words (`unicode-segmentation`) or chars for CJK. Severity: low.

44. **`src-tauri/capabilities/desktop.json:8,10` — `"clipboard-manager:default"` is listed twice; and `default.json:10` grants `opener:default` alongside the scoped `opener:allow-open-url` — verify the default set doesn't already grant a broader open-url scope that makes the explicit allowlist moot.** Fix: dedupe and grant only the scoped permission. Severity: low.

**Notable things verified as fine:** WAL + foreign_keys pragmas and sensible indices in db.rs; atomic temp-file+rename for model downloads with size validation; updater pubkey pinning present; AppleScript strings only built for allowlisted bundle IDs (no injection); osascript bounded by an 800 ms deadline; `get_frontmost_app`/`list_installed_apps` correctly use `spawn_blocking`; PostHog payloads contain no transcription text; the panic hook logs location before aborting.</result>

<result># VoxFusion UX Audit — Findings (code-derived, ordered by severity)

## High

1. **Core dictation — transcription failure is completely silent and the dictation is lost from the user's POV.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:311-314` — on `transcribeAudio` error the handler only logs and `return`s; the spinner clears, the pill hides (`:343`), no error UI, no retry, and `saveTranscription` never runs so nothing appears in history. Problem: the user speaks, sees the spinner, then everything vanishes with zero explanation and no way to recover the take (the WAV survives on disk but no UI exposes it). Improvement: show a failure state in the pill (or a system notification) with a "Retry transcription" action wired to the preserved WAV path. **Severity: high.**

2. **Core dictation — recording that fails to start is also silent.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:410-417` — `startRecordingWithDevice` error → log, hide window, return; and `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:99-102` errors with "No input device found with name: …" when the saved mic is unplugged, with no fallback to the default device. Problem: pressing the hotkey with a missing/unplugged selected mic does literally nothing visible, which reads as "the app is broken". Improvement: fall back to the system default input when the named device is absent, and surface a one-line error in the pill/notification when start fails. **Severity: high.**

3. **Onboarding — denying microphone permission is a hard dead-end.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/onboarding/steps/MicrophonePermissionStep.tsx:35-51` re-calls `getUserMedia`, but once macOS TCC has denied it every retry auto-fails; unlike the accessibility step there is no "Open System Settings" link, and `OnboardingWizard.tsx:63-70` blocks Next until granted (no skip). Problem: a user who clicks "Don't Allow" once is stuck on step 1 forever with a button that appears to do nothing. Improvement: detect the `denied` permission state and swap the button to a deep link to System Settings → Privacy → Microphone with instructions (mirroring `AccessibilityPermissionStep`). **Severity: high.**

4. **Onboarding — the ~1.5 GB model download is not resumable, not cancellable, and shows no speed/ETA/bytes.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/models.rs:183-189` deletes any partial file before every attempt and has no Range/resume support or cancel command; `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/onboarding/steps/ModelDownloadStep.tsx:93-98` shows only a percentage; `:120-126` "Retry Download" restarts from 0%. Problem: on a flaky or slow connection users repeatedly lose 1.5 GB of progress and can neither pause nor estimate completion. Improvement: add HTTP Range resume of the `.download.tmp` file, a cancel button, and show MB downloaded + speed + ETA. **Severity: high.**

5. **Trust — PostHog analytics run unconditionally with no consent, disclosure, or opt-out anywhere in the UI.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/lib/posthog.ts:25-39` initializes with a hardcoded key at `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/index.tsx:19`; events include `transcription_copied` with `transcription_id`/`text_length` (`TranscriptionCard.tsx:26-29`) and pageviews; the `sidebar.privacy` string exists in `en.ts:305` but is never rendered, and Settings (`SettingsSidebar`/`SettingsModal.tsx:26-32`) has no privacy section. Problem: an app marketed as "local, offline transcription" (`en.ts:437-445`) phones home with usage telemetry the user never agreed to or can disable. Improvement: add a Privacy settings section with an analytics toggle (calling `posthog.opt_out_capturing()`) and disclose collection during onboarding. **Severity: high.**

6. **Trust/edge case — every raw dictation WAV is kept on disk forever with no cleanup or UI.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:244-258` writes `app_data/recordings/<timestamp>.wav`; nothing deletes them (only `parakeet.rs:95` removes its own resample temp), and cancel (`VoiceControl.tsx:375`) also leaves the file. Problem: unbounded disk growth and an undisclosed archive of everything the user has ever said near their machine. Improvement: delete the WAV after successful transcription (or add a retention setting + "clear recordings" button in Settings). **Severity: high.**

7. **Core dictation — accessibility revocation after onboarding fails silently; the recovery event is dead code.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/App.tsx:150-154` listens for `accessibility-permission-needed`, but no code anywhere emits it (grep over `src/` and `src-tauri/` finds only the listener); `VoiceControl.tsx:325` ignores the `typeText` Result, so an `enigo` failure (`handlers/text.rs:5-9`) surfaces nowhere. Problem: if the user (or a macOS update) revokes Accessibility, dictation transcribes but never types, with no prompt to re-grant. Improvement: check `typeText`'s Result and, on failure, probe `check_accessibility_probe` and emit/handle `accessibility-permission-needed` to open Settings with guidance. **Severity: high.**

8. **Core dictation — the Whisper model (1.5 GB) is reloaded from disk on every single transcription.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:175-177` constructs `WhisperContext::new_with_params(&model_path, …)` inside `transcribe_audio` with no caching. Problem: every dictation pays multi-second model-load latency while the user stares at an indeterminate spinner (`VoiceControl.tsx:481`). Improvement: cache the loaded `WhisperContext` in managed state (invalidate on `active-model-changed`). **Severity: high.**

## Medium

9. **Settings — hotkey validation is purely structural; no conflict detection against system shortcuts or between the two app hotkeys.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/lib/hotkeyUtils.ts:366-381` only checks "modifiers + one key"; nothing rejects e.g. `Command+Q` or `Command+Space`; and if both hotkeys are recorded identical, `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:172` silently registers only the toggle handler, dropping hold-to-speak with no warning. Problem: users can hijack critical OS shortcuts or unknowingly disable hold-to-speak. Improvement: add a deny-list of well-known system shortcuts plus an explicit "both hotkeys are identical — hold-to-speak disabled" inline warning. **Severity: medium.**

10. **Core dictation — Escape is registered as a system-wide global shortcut for the entire duration of every recording.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:347-354` `register("Escape", …)` on record start. Problem: while dictating, Escape is swallowed from the frontmost app (can't close dialogs/menus/vim-mode etc.), and the user gets no hint that Escape now means "cancel dictation". Improvement: capture Escape via the existing NSEvent watcher (observe-only, non-swallowing) or scope cancel to a modifier combo, and show "ESC to cancel" in the pill. **Severity: medium.**

11. **Core dictation — pressing any regular key during hold-to-speak silently cancels and discards the recording.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:252-259` — any `keyboard-key-pressed` (except Escape) while `recordingMode() === "hold"` calls `cancelInterruptedHoldToSpeakRecording` (`:158-163`), which discards the audio. Problem: brushing a key while holding RightCommand throws away the whole utterance without transcribing or explaining. Improvement: stop-and-transcribe on interruption instead of cancel, or flash a "cancelled" state in the pill. **Severity: medium.**

12. **Discoverability — the Home screen's hotkey hint is hard-coded to the default hotkey and ignores the user's configured one.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/i18n/translations/en.ts:219` "Press Left Control+Left Option to start a new recording" and `:292-293` (empty-state), rendered verbatim at `Home.tsx:25` and `TranscriptionList.tsx:158`. Problem: a user who set a custom hotkey in onboarding is shown wrong instructions on the main screen — the single post-onboarding reminder of how to dictate. Improvement: interpolate `hotkeyDisplayName(settings().hotkey)` into these strings as `LearningStep.tsx:36` already does. **Severity: medium.**

13. **Updates — the download progress bar is mathematically broken, and there is no changelog or dismiss control.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/UpdateNotification.tsx:103-105` accumulates raw chunk *bytes* into `downloadProgress`, then `:152` renders `width: min(bytes/10, 100)%` — it pegs at 100% after ~1 KB; `update.body` (release notes) is never rendered and the `update.ignore` string (`en.ts:451`) is unused, so the banner is permanent. Problem: the progress bar lies (full instantly, then minutes of "downloading"), and users can neither see what's in the update nor dismiss the notice. Improvement: compute percent from `contentLength`, render `update()?.body` as a changelog, and add a dismiss/skip-version button. Update is optional (good) — reachable via menu "Check for Updates" (`menu.rs:19-25`). **Severity: medium.**

14. **Settings/onboarding — model downloads have no in-flight guard, so duplicate concurrent downloads of the same file are possible.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/models.rs:173-235` has no per-model download lock; UI state is component-local, so closing the Settings modal (`ModelSettings.tsx:21-23`) or navigating Back/Next in onboarding (`ModelDownloadStep.tsx:19-21`) remounts with `isDownloading=false` and shows the "Download" button again while the first download still streams — clicking it opens a second writer on the same `.download.tmp`. Problem: progress UI is lost on remount and re-clicking can corrupt the temp file. Improvement: track in-flight downloads in Rust state, reject duplicates, and have the UI derive "downloading" from a queryable backend state/event replay. **Severity: medium.**

15. **Onboarding — the accessibility step force-marks the permission granted when the probe still says no.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/onboarding/steps/AccessibilityPermissionStep.tsx:61-68` — after the distributed notification `com.apple.accessibility.api` (which fires for *any* app's AX toggle, `accessibility_watcher.rs:33-41`) and four failed probes, `markGranted()` is called anyway. Problem: toggling accessibility for some other app while VoxFusion is untrusted lets the user pass step 2 with a permission they don't have, deferring the failure to a silent typing error later (finding 7). Improvement: only trust the notification when a follow-up `AXIsProcessTrusted` probe eventually succeeds; otherwise keep polling and show "still waiting for macOS…". **Severity: medium.**

16. **Onboarding — a failed practice transcription in the learning step shows nothing; the error string exists but is never used.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/onboarding/steps/LearningStep.tsx:58-64` only listens for `transcription-created` (success); `onboarding.learningError` ("Transcription failed. Try again.", `en.ts:435`) is referenced nowhere. Problem: if the first-ever dictation fails, the new user waits at step 6 with no feedback, and the only way forward (typing manually into the chat box) is undiscoverable. Improvement: listen for a transcription-failed event and render `learningError`, plus a visible "skip this step" affordance. **Severity: medium.**

17. **Overlay — positioned against full monitor bounds (not the visible work area) and cannot be moved.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:93-96` uses `monitor.size` with a fixed `BOTTOM_PADDING = 20` (`:51`), placing the 28 px pill ~20 px above the raw screen bottom — inside the macOS Dock's region; there is no drag region or position preference (`window.rs:8-24`). Problem: with a visible Dock the pill can be overlapped/obscured, and users who dislike the location can't move it. Improvement: use the monitor's work area (or add Dock-height padding) and offer a position preference or draggable pill. Positives verified: it correctly follows the cursor's monitor (`:81-97`, 1 s poll `:186`), never steals focus (`window.rs:22 focused(false)`), and buttons work without focus (`accept_first_mouse(true)`). **Severity: medium.**

18. **Non-English dictation — there is no way to set the transcription language; the UI language setting doesn't affect it.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:191-199` auto-detects language per utterance (falling back to a default locale on failure); `LanguageSettings.tsx:26-28` is explicitly "INTERFACE_LANGUAGE" only. Problem: auto-detect is fine usually, but on short or accented utterances it misfires and the user has no override, and nothing in the UI explains which language will be transcribed. Improvement: add a "Transcription language: Auto / <list>" setting in the Model or Language section, passed to `params.set_language`. **Severity: medium.**

19. **Recording — a mic stream error mid-recording (device unplugged while speaking) is swallowed.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/handlers/audio.rs:122-124` `err_fn` only `eprintln!`s; the pill keeps animating on the idle wave pattern (`VoiceControl.tsx:119-124` renders even with `audioLevel = 0`). Problem: the user keeps talking into a dead stream and gets an empty/garbage transcription with no warning. Improvement: emit a `recording-error` event from `err_fn` and transition the pill to an error state. **Severity: medium.**

## Low

20. **Tray — the Microphone submenu is empty on first launch until any settings change fires.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src-tauri/src/tray.rs:48` builds the submenu with `vec![]` devices; items are only appended inside the `settings-changed` listener (`:100-135`). Problem: a fresh user opening the tray sees a dead "Microphone" submenu. Improvement: enumerate devices at tray setup time. **Severity: low.**

21. **Tray — no recording indicator; the tray icon is static.**
Evidence: `tray.rs:58-63` sets one template icon and never updates it; no menu item shows recording state or the hotkey. Problem: in tray, there is no ambient signal that the mic is live (the only indicator is the small pill). Improvement: swap the tray icon (or add a menu line) while recording. **Severity: low.**

22. **History — transcriptions can only be copied: no delete, search, or full-text view.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/components/TranscriptionCard.tsx:46-49` truncates at 150 chars with no expand; the card's only action is Copy (`:66-77`); no delete command exists in `lib.rs:57-101`'s handler list. Problem: long dictations can't be read in full and sensitive history can't be removed. Improvement: add expand-on-click, per-item delete, and a "clear history" control. **Severity: low.**

23. **Dictionary/Style — no bulk operations or import/export anywhere.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/DictionaryDefault.tsx` (single-word add/edit/delete only) and equivalents in `DictionaryPerApp.tsx`/`DictionarySites.tsx`; no export/import commands in `lib.rs`. Problem: users with existing term lists must enter words one at a time and can't back up or move configurations between machines. Improvement: paste-multiple / CSV import-export on the dictionary tabs. Positives: empty states are good (`DictionaryDefault.tsx:116-128`), `AddSiteForm.tsx:8-20` normalizes pasted URLs well, and unconfigured apps are searchable with keyboard nav (`DictionaryPerApp.tsx:116-138`). **Severity: low.**

24. **Discoverability — Dictionary and Style are never introduced; onboarding ends without mentioning them.**
Evidence: `CompletionStep.tsx` says only "You're all set" (`:20-24`); nothing links to `/dictionary` or `/style`. Problem: the app's differentiating features rely on the user spontaneously clicking sidebar items 02/03. Improvement: add one completion-step line ("Boost accuracy with your Dictionary →") or a first-run hint on Home. **Severity: low.**

25. **Overlay — the reposition poll (`cursorPosition` + `monitorFromPoint`) runs every second forever, even while the window is hidden.**
Evidence: `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:185-187`. Problem: constant background IPC/wakeups for a window that is invisible ~99% of the time (battery cost on laptops). # VoxFusion Frontend Audit — `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/src`

**Framework: SolidJS** (confirmed via `package.json` deps `solid-js`/`vite-plugin-solid`/`@solidjs/router`, `vite.config.ts` `plugins: [solid()]`, and `render()` from `solid-js/web` in `index.tsx`). The README claim is correct — but several bugs below are React idioms that silently do nothing in Solid.

All paths below are under `/Users/egortokarev/Code/voxfusion/packages/app/` (line numbers refer to the files there).

---

## HIGH

1. **`src/pages/VoiceControl.tsx:100,309` — the overlay window transcribes with the wrong style: `settings()` is never initialized in this window.** `initSettings()` is only called in `src/App.tsx:94` (main window); the voice-control window is a separate JS context, so `useSettings()` returns `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` forever, and `transcribeAudio(..., settings().defaultStyle)` always passes `"default"`, ignoring the user's configured default style (line 322 also logs the wrong style). Fix: keep a local `defaultStyle` signal fed from `loadSettings()` in `onMount` and refreshed in the existing `settings-changed` listener (which already updates mic/mute but forgot style).

2. **`src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:81-92` — React-ism: `createEffect` "returns a cleanup function", which Solid treats as an accumulator value, never a cleanup.** `return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleEscape)` never runs, so every modal open adds another permanent window `keydown` listener (and Escape keeps firing `onClose` even when the modal is closed). Fix: `onCleanup(() => window.removeEventListener(...))` inside the effect.

3. **`src/components/settings/ModelSettings.tsx:35-46` — `onCleanup` registered after `await` inside an async `onMount` runs outside the reactive owner and never executes**, so the `"model-download-progress"` listener leaks every time the Model section is opened (the component is unmounted/remounted by the `<Show>` in `SettingsModal.tsx:139`). Each leaked handler keeps mutating a disposed component's signals and calling `refresh()`. Fix: register a synchronous `onCleanup` with an `unlisten` variable + `disposed` flag (the correct pattern already exists in `UpdateNotification.tsx:64-80`).

4. **`src/components/onboarding/steps/ModelDownloadStep.tsx:33-41` — same bug family: `onCleanup(() => unlisten())` after two `await`s is a no-op**, leaking a `"model-download-progress"` listener each time step 5 mounts (navigating Back/Next in the wizard remounts it). Same fix as #3.

5. **`src/components/UpdateNotification.tsx:104,152 — update progress bar is mathematically meaningless.** `const progress = downloadProgress() + event.data.chunkLength;` accumulates raw **bytes** into the signal, and the bar renders `width: ${Math.min(downloadProgress() / 10, 100)}%` — i.e. full after 1,000 bytes; `event.data.contentLength` (line 95) is checked but never stored, and `downloadedBytes` (line 91) duplicates the signal. Fix: capture `contentLength` on `Started` and set `progress = downloadedBytes / contentLength * 100`.

input.content:
# VoxFusion Improvement Audit — 2026-07-02

Produced by a five-track deep audit (Rust backend, app frontend, product UX, marketing site, tooling/CI/docs). Every finding was verified against the actual code — line numbers are current as of commit `b0135b8`. ~190 unique findings after deduplication.

Severity: **H** = high (user-facing breakage, security/privacy, trust), **M** = medium, **L** = low.

---

## Top priorities (start here)

1. **Cache the Whisper model** — the ~1.5 GB model is loaded from disk on *every* transcription (`src-tauri/src/handlers/whisper.rs:176`), adding multi-second latency to every dictation. Cache `WhisperContext` in Tauri managed state, invalidate on model switch. Single biggest perceived-performance win in the product.
2. **Make the core dictation loop stop failing silently** — one theme, many sites: transcription errors vanish with no UI (`VoiceControl.tsx:311-314`), recording-start failures do nothing visible (`VoiceControl.tsx:410-417`), a mic unplugged mid-recording is swallowed by `eprintln!` (`audio.rs:122-124`), and a revoked Accessibility permission means text silently never types — the recovery event `accessibility-permission-needed` is listened for (`App.tsx:150-154`) but *never emitted anywhere*. Add an error state to the overlay pill + a retry path (the WAV survives on disk).
3. **Fix the recording state latch** — any error after `is_recording.store(true)` (`audio.rs:87`) leaves the recorder latched; every later dictation fails with "Recording is already in progress" until restart. Use a drop-guard that resets the flag on error paths.
4. **The overlay window ignores the user's default style** — `initSettings()` only runs in the main window; the voice-control window is a separate JS context, so `settings().defaultStyle` is always `"default"` (`VoiceControl.tsx:100,309`). User-facing data bug on every transcription.
5. **Close the security holes as a set** — `"csp": null` (`tauri.conf.json:44`) + every system-wide keystroke broadcast into the webview (`system_key_watcher.rs:133-146`) + `read_audio_file` accepting arbitrary absolute paths (`handlers/text.rs:12`) compose into: any webview compromise = system keylogger + arbitrary file exfiltration. Set a CSP, match hotkeys in Rust, and restrict paths to the recordings dir.
6. **Tell one honest privacy story** — the product's positioning ("local-first, 0 data sent to servers") is contradicted by: PostHog running unconditionally with no consent or opt-out (`src/lib/posthog.ts:25-39`), every dictation WAV kept on disk forever with no cleanup (`audio.rs:244-258`), the marketing hero stat "0 data sent to servers", a privacy policy that never names PostHog/Umami, and a README claiming "no servers". Fix together: analytics opt-out toggle + onboarding disclosure, WAV deletion after transcription (or retention setting), reworded marketing claims ("0 *audio* sent to servers"), updated policy.
7. **Harden the 1.5 GB model download** — not resumable (partial deleted before every retry, `models.rs:183-189`), not cancellable, no checksum (URL pins mutable `resolve/main`), no in-flight guard (double-click = two writers on the same temp file), 1-hour *total* timeout kills slow connections, and progress events fire per chunk (hundreds of thousands of IPC events). Add Range resume, cancel, SHA-256 + pinned revision, per-model in-flight lock, and emit on whole-percent change.
8. **`panic = "abort"` defeats every `catch_unwind`** (`Cargo.toml:62` vs `apps.rs:238,270,347`) — a malformed `Info.plist`/`.icns` in /Applications, or an ObjC exception in `get_frontmost_app` (runs at the start of *every* dictation), aborts the whole app in release. Drop `panic = "abort"` or stop relying on catch_unwind.
9. **Hotkeys permanently die if Accessibility isn't granted at first watcher start** — `addGlobalMonitorForEventsMatchingMask_handler` returns `None`, it's silently forgotten, and the `WATCHER_RUNNING` latch blocks all retries until app restart (`system_key_watcher.rs:160,176-193`).
10. **Onboarding dead-end: denied microphone permission** — no "Open System Settings" link and no skip; once macOS TCC denies, every retry auto-fails and the user is stuck on step 1 forever (`MicrophonePermissionStep.tsx:35-51`).
11. **Marketing says the wrong hotkey** — site teaches `Cmd+;` in three places (`i18n/ru/hero.ts:6`, `features.ts:8`, `index.astro:83`); the app default is `LeftControl+LeftOption` (`hotkeyUtils.ts:44`). Also: Terms prohibit decompiling / competing products for an MIT-licensed app with a public repo — direct license contradiction.
12. **No CI whatsoever** — no PR checks, and `release.yml` ships from a tag with zero lint/typecheck/test gates. Add a `ci.yml` (biome, tsc, astro check, vite build on ubuntu; `cargo check`/`cargo test` on macos) and make release depend on it.
13. **Update progress bar is mathematically broken** — raw chunk *bytes* accumulate into the percent signal and render as `width: bytes/10 %`, pegging at 100% after ~1 KB (`UpdateNotification.tsx:103-105,152`); `contentLength` is checked but never stored. Also no changelog shown, no dismiss button.

### Quick wins (minutes each, big payoff)

- **One-file tsconfig fix kills all ~1157 `astro check` errors**: marketingsite tsconfig inherits the root's repo-wide `include` + `jsx: "react-jsx"`, so it type-checks the app's Solid TSX as React. Change to `"extends": "astro/tsconfigs/strict"`, `"include": ["src", ".astro/types.d.ts"]`.
- **Two-line biome.json override makes `bun run lint` exit clean**: add `noUnusedImports: off` + `useImportType: off` to the `**/*.astro` override.
- **Docs' first command is broken**: `bun run tauri:dev` doesn't exist (README:50, CONTRIBUTING:33, AGENTS:20) — the script is `dev`.
- **Home-screen hotkey hint is hardcoded to the default hotkey** (`en.ts:219,292-293`) — users with a custom hotkey are shown wrong instructions on the main screen. Interpolate `hotkeyDisplayName(settings().hotkey)` as `LearningStep.tsx:36` already does.
- **`bun install --frozen-lockfile`** in release.yml:40 and the Dockerfile.
- **Remove the squatting-risk updater endpoint** — `tauri.conf.json:50-53` tries `github.com/voxfusion/voxfusion` first, an org that doesn't match the actual repo owner.

---

## A. Desktop app — Rust backend (src-tauri)

### High
- **A1 (H)** `Cargo.toml:62` + `apps.rs:238,270,347` — `panic = "abort"` makes `catch_unwind` useless; malformed plist/icns or ObjC exception aborts the app (see Top #8).
- **A2 (H)** `audio.rs:87` — errors after `is_recording.store(true)` latch the recorder forever (see Top #3).
- **A3 (H)** `whisper.rs:176` — model loaded from disk every transcription (see Top #1).
- **A4 (H)** `system_key_watcher.rs:133-146` — every global keydown's keycode emitted into the webview; with no CSP this is a keylogger stream. Match chords in Rust or emit only during hotkey recording.
- **A5 (H)** `tauri.conf.json:44` — `"csp": null`. Set a CSP restricted to `'self'` + PostHog origin.
- **A6 (H)** `audio.rs:121-124` — cpal stream errors (mic disconnect) swallowed by `eprintln!`; UI keeps showing "recording". Emit a `recording-error` event and finalize.
- **A7 (H)** `system_key_watcher.rs:160,176-193` — watcher install failure silently forgotten + `WATCHER_RUNNING` latch prevents retry (see Top #9).

### Medium
- **A8 (M)** `audio.rs:210-235` — stop takes the writer *before* pausing the stream; audio tail between the two is dropped — users lose the last word. Pause/drop stream first.
- **A9 (M)** `audio.rs:290,298` — callback drops whole chunks on `try_lock` failure and swallows write errors; disk-full = silently corrupt WAV. Use a lock-free channel + surface write failures.
- **A10 (M)** `audio.rs:16-19` — `unsafe impl Send/Sync for SafeStream` overrides cpal's deliberate `!Send`/`!Sync` with no justification; stream is created and dropped on different tokio workers. Own the stream on a dedicated thread driven by a channel.
- **A11 (M)** Sync commands block the main thread: `audio_processing.rs:4` (full WAV decode+resample), `text.rs:12` (whole-file read), `text.rs:5` (enigo types entire transcription while the event loop is frozen). Make async + `spawn_blocking`.
- **A12 (M)** `audio_processing.rs:4`, `text.rs:12` — `Vec<u8>` returned as JSON number arrays over IPC (~4× size). Return `tauri::ipc::Response::new(bytes)`.
- **A13 (M)** `whisper.rs:189-320`, `parakeet.rs:84-93` — seconds-to-minutes of inference runs inline on a tokio worker, starving the runtime. Wrap in `spawn_blocking` / `tokio::process`.
- **A14 (M)** `parakeet.rs:84-93` — `Command::output()` with no timeout; hung engine hangs transcription forever (browser.rs osascript gets 800 ms — apply same discipline).
- **A15 (M)** `parakeet.rs:41` + `entitlements.plist:13` — engine falls back to `$PATH` resolution and `disable-library-validation` lets the app load unsigned dylibs from user-writable app-data; any same-user process can plant a `crispasr` binary. Drop the PATH fallback, sign the engine, remove the entitlement.
- **A16 (M)** `entitlements.plist:7,9,13` — `allow-unsigned-executable-memory` is a superset of `allow-jit` and likely neither is needed. Empirically trim.
- **A17 (M)** `models.rs` — no in-flight download guard; concurrent downloads interleave into the same `.download.tmp` (see Top #7).
- **A18 (M)** `models.rs:53,66,109` — no checksum; URL pins mutable `resolve/main`; only size is checked. Pin a revision hash + verify SHA-256.
- **A19 (M)** `models.rs:192,211,222` — 1-hour total request timeout, blocking `std::fs` on the runtime, no Range resume (see Top #7).
- **A20 (M)** `models.rs:234` — progress emitted per chunk. Emit on integer-percent change.
- **A21 (M)** `audio.rs:243-258` — recordings written to app-data forever; nothing deletes them (see Top #6).
- **A22 (M)** `text.rs:12-14` (+ `audio_processing.rs:4`, whisper `audio_path`) — commands accept arbitrary absolute paths from the webview; generic file-read primitive. Canonicalize + require paths inside the recordings dir.
- **A23 (M)** `posthog.ts:25-39` / `index.tsx:19` — analytics with no opt-out (see Top #6). Payloads verified metadata-only.
- **A24 (M)** `lib.rs:143-148` — single-instance plugin registered inside `.setup()` with `let _ =`; must be the *first* plugin registered, and errors are swallowed.
- **A25 (M)** `tray.rs:80,107` — CoreAudio device enumeration runs synchronously on the main thread in menu handlers; errors discarded.
- **A26 (M)** `apps.rs:560+` — `list_installed_apps` re-scans three dirs and re-decodes every `.icns`→PNG→base64 on every call, no cache. Cache keyed by path+mtime.
- **A27 (M)** `capabilities/desktop.json:14` — `core:webview:allow-internal-toggle-devtools` granted in production capability.
- **A28 (M)** `media.rs` — crash/quit between mute and restore leaves system output muted; default-output change mid-recording unmutes the wrong device. Restore in `RunEvent::Exit`, remember the device id.
- **A29 (M)** `tauri.conf.json:50-53` — updater endpoint #1 points at a GitHub org that isn't yours (see Quick wins).

### Low
- **A30 (L)** `audio.rs:255` — second-resolution filenames; two recordings in one second overwrite. Add ms/UUID.
- **A31 (L)** `db.rs:261`, `apps.rs:598`, `sites.rs:184` — updates return `created_at: String::new()`. Use `RETURNING`.
- **A32 (L)** `db.rs:118+` — cursor pagination on `created_at < ?` skips rows sharing a timestamp. Composite `(created_at, id)` cursor.
- **A33 (L)** `db.rs:73` — only index on `dictionary_words` is on `word`, which no query uses; queries order by `created_at`.
